config.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals

intro.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page website using Next.js 13+ App Router to understand its file-based routing system. You'll learn how to create pages by adding React components to the `app` directory, where each folder automatically becomes a route. The core concept is dynamic routing, where you'll use special files like `page.js` and `layout.js` to structure your application. You'll work with React components, JSX, and Next.js-specific features to navigate between pages seamlessly. By the end, you'll have a functional site with multiple routes, demonstrating the fundamentals of the App Router.
intro.usecase: The Next.js App Router is the foundation for building modern web applications with complex navigation and data loading patterns. You'll see this in e-commerce platforms like Amazon where product pages, search results, and user dashboards are separate routes with different data requirements. Content-heavy sites like news portals or blogs use App Router features for dynamic routing to articles, category pages, and author profiles. Developers implement this pattern when building admin dashboards with nested layouts, authentication-protected routes, and server-side data fetching for real-time analytics.

objectives: Construct a Next.js application using the App Router structure
Configure dynamic routes with parameters in the App Router
Implement page components with server-side rendering capabilities
Initialize and integrate layout components that persist across routes
Apply loading and error boundary patterns within the App Router
Manipulate navigation between pages using Next.js Link components
Render nested layouts for complex application structures

steps.title: Import Next.js App Router components and React hooks
steps.instruction: Import Link from 'next/link', useRouter from 'next/router', and React from 'react' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the required modules. Remember to import React even if you don't use it directly in JSX.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Link, useRouter, and React here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for Next.js App Router functionality are added to the file.
successCriteria: Link is imported from 'next/link', useRouter is imported from 'next/router', and React is imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required modules. Make sure to import Link from 'next/link', useRouter from 'next/router', and React from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Link from 'next/link', useRouter from 'next/router', and React from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main page component
steps.instruction: Create a default export function component named HomePage that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called HomePage and export it as default. The function should return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: A HomePage component is created and exported as default, returning null.
successCriteria: HomePage function is defined and exported as default, returning null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the HomePage component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named HomePage and exported it as default.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined a function named HomePage and exported it as default.

steps.title: Initialize router instance for navigation
steps.instruction: Inside the HomePage component, call the useRouter hook and store the result in a variable named router.
steps.hint: The useRouter hook returns an object with routing methods and properties. Call it at the top of your component body.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: calling a hook and storing its result
const router = useRouter();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a router variable initialized with the Next.js router object, ready for navigation operations.
successCriteria: The useRouter hook is called and its return value is stored in a variable named router.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useRouter() and storing the result in a variable named router inside the component body.
steps.feedbackWrong: call the useRouter hook and store its return value in a variable named router at the top of your HomePage component.

steps.title: Create navigation handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the HomePage component, create a function named handleNavigate that uses the router variable to navigate to the '/about' page.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls router.push('/about') when invoked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleNavigate function is defined and ready to be called for navigation.
successCriteria: A function named handleNavigate exists inside HomePage and calls router.push('/about').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named handleNavigate and calls router.push('/about').
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleNavigate function isn't properly defined. Create a function that uses router.push('/about') for navigation.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside your HomePage component, return a main element with className='container'.
steps.hint: The main element should be the top-level JSX element returned by your component.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component now returns a main element with the 'container' class, providing a wrapper for the page content.
successCriteria: The HomePage component returns a main element with className='container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a main element with exactly className='container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Your component should return a main element with className='container'.

steps.title: Add page title and description
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add an h1 element with the text 'Next.js App Router' and a p element with the text 'Learn the fundamentals of Next.js routing'.
steps.hint: Add the h1 and p elements as direct children of the main element. The h1 should come first, then the p.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding static content

Page Title

This is a description.
steps.expectedOutcome: The page will display a heading 'Next.js App Router' and a paragraph with the description.
successCriteria: The main container contains an h1 element with the exact text 'Next.js App Router' and a p element with the exact text 'Learn the fundamentals of Next.js routing'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some content, but make sure both the h1 and p elements are present with the exact text specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required h1 and p elements with the specified text are not found in the main container.

steps.title: Create navigation section with Link component
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add a <nav> section containing a Link component that navigates to '/about' with the text 'Go to About Page'.
steps.hint: Use the Link component you imported earlier. The Link should have an href attribute pointing to '/about' and contain the text content.
steps.analogousExample:
// Navigation section example
<nav>
  <Link href="/about">Go to About Page</Link>
</nav>
steps.expectedOutcome: A navigation section appears inside the main container with a working Link to the About page.
successCriteria: The main container contains a <nav> element with a Link component that has href="/about" and displays 'Go to About Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a <nav> element containing a Link with href="/about" and the text 'Go to About Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation section is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added a <nav> element with a Link component inside the main container.

steps.title: Add programmatic navigation button
steps.instruction: Inside the main container, add a button element with the text 'Navigate Programmatically' and wire its onClick event to the handleNavigate function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> JSX element with an onClick prop that references your existing handleNavigate function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Navigate Programmatically' appears in the UI that, when clicked, will navigate to the /about page.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Navigate Programmatically' is added inside the main container, and its onClick prop is set to handleNavigate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing either the correct text or the onClick handler. Make sure the button says 'Navigate Programmatically' and has onClick={handleNavigate}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly implemented. Check that you've added a <button> element with the correct text and onClick handler inside the main container.

steps.title: Display current route information
steps.instruction: Inside your component, add a paragraph element that displays the current path using router.pathname
steps.hint: Access the pathname property from your router instance and display it within JSX curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value from an object in JSX

Current value: {someObject.property}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current path (like '/') in a paragraph when you run the app.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists that displays router.pathname within JSX curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're accessing router.pathname and displaying it within a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The current route information isn't displayed correctly. Check that you're using router.pathname inside JSX curly braces within a paragraph element.

steps.title: Add styling to the navigation elements
steps.instruction: Add className='nav-link' to the Link component and className='nav-button' to the button in your navigation section.
steps.hint: Add the className attribute to both the Link and button elements with the specified values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Link and button elements will have the specified CSS class names for styling.
successCriteria: The Link component has className='nav-link' and the button has className='nav-button'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added one of the class names, but both the Link and button need their respective className attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation elements don't have the required className attributes. Make sure to add className='nav-link' to the Link and className='nav-button' to the button.
